facts.excerpt: An Energy Ball. Can be picked up in the Citadel or if a Combine Elite fires one.
facts.observations: The page describes ordinary primary fire punting held objects, normal object manipulation, the Citadel confiscation field supercharging the Gravity Gun, and capture of Combine energy balls. The actual article warns that it may contain errors; it is a secondary wiki, not a frame-accurate official animation source.
facts.adaptation: An orange tool prop punt and a blue Citadel tool redirecting one captured energy ball remain distinct. Source-game lethal/vaporizing effects are replaced by one bounded projectile impact, with no thrown human body or continuous emitted laser. The kit drops the Half-Life1 Gluon Gun.

facts.excerpt: Pulse Rifle (HL2, Ep1); Civil Protection gear (HL2)
facts.observations: The page distinguishes the earlier Black Mesa security guard from the Half-Life2 undercover Civil Protection officer and Resistance leader.
facts.adaptation: The selected unmasked Civil Protection clothing and AR2 replace the old blue guard uniform and pistol. Rifle damage and the allied coordination bonus are bounded authored values.

facts.excerpt: Alyx easily conceals it inside her jacket, and uses it often to defeat hostiles alongside Gordon.
facts.observations: The article describes the actual Alyx handgun, its compact black casing, extended magazine and Half-Life2 use; it distinguishes the Half-Life:Alyx upgrade history.
facts.adaptation: One finite physical pistol shot replaces the unrelated holographic dog and gravity glove shown or named in the old kit. Door-opening support is an explicit role adaptation without offensive hacking damage.

facts.excerpt: Scientist / Resistance leader (HL2); replaces his missing left leg beneath the knee
facts.observations: The article identifies Eli as a researcher and Resistance coordinator at Black Mesa East, developing teleportation and the Gravity Gun. It identifies his left below-knee prosthetic leg. An in-game image search result from this wiki corroborated the vest and Harvard shirt design; no live actor portrait was supplied.
facts.adaptation: The selected notebook/radio briefing is zero-damage allied support. Its numerical buff is not a canonical named power. The old invented laser weapon is removed.

facts.excerpt: A teleportation system, developed jointly by Kleiner and Vance, allows for near-instantaneous travel
facts.observations: The read article describes Kleiner operating his physical laboratory and preparing travel between the two Resistance labs. It also describes a shotgun late in the story; this selection intentionally uses his non-offensive laboratory role.
facts.adaptation: Physical notes and control-box calibration represent a zero-damage allied guard adaptation. No handheld energy gun, projected portal attack, healing or magical shielding equipment is claimed.

facts.excerpt: Paladin Danse | Laser Gun; Nick Valentine | Pipe Revolver; Piper Wright | 10mm Pistol; Preston Garvey | Laser Musket
facts.observations: The actual default-weapon table was opened and read. It supports Danse’s laser rifle, Nick’s pipe revolver, Piper’s10mm pistol and Preston’s laser musket. It does not prove exact weapon meshes, calibres, costume pixels or animation frames.
facts.adaptation: Nick’s name does not assert a .44 calibre. All selected gun supers are finite single-target shots. Piper’s information super stays zero-damage allied support. No Liberty Prime summon or weaponized case file is retained.

facts.observations: The companion table was actually read. It independently identifies Dogmeat as the Red Rocket companion and lists the armed companions’ general weapons. This page does not establish every selected animation or canine attack timing.
facts.adaptation: Dogmeat’s canine bite/hold, the companion support percentages and finite attack timing are project adaptations. Dogmeat is always a quadruped without hands or weapons, calibrated separately from humanoids.
